_comment: DSH MCP config for browser control. Merge into your DSH MCP settings, then RESTART DSH. This machine has NO Google Chrome, so the server is pointed at Edge via --executablePath (Edge is Chromium-based and speaks the same CDP protocol). With --executablePath the MCP launches and manages the browser itself - you do NOT need to start Edge or the debug port manually.
_c_drive_avoidance: This machine's C: is nearly full, so every browser-related cache is redirected to E:. --userDataDir keeps the MCP browser profile off C:. The npm cache is redirected via `npm config set cache E:\dsh-cache\npm-cache`, and Playwright's binaries live in E:\ms-playwright via the user env var PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH.
_alternative_browserUrl: To instead attach to an ALREADY-RUNNING browser (window stays visible, reuses your logged-in profile), drop --executablePath and use --browser-url=http://127.0.0.1:9222, after starting Edge with ALL windows closed: "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe" --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir="E:\dsh-cache\dsh-edge-profile"  (the default profile refuses to open a debug port on newer builds). Ready check: http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version returns JSON.
_note_npx: npx.ps1 is blocked by PowerShell execution policy on this machine, so invoke the npx.cmd shim through cmd /c instead of bare 'npx'.
